title: Suffix Length Comparison
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $x$. For every decomposition $x=ps$ into Boolean words and every natural number $r$ with $r\le |c.output|$, the captured-length checker, started from the configuration built from $c$ in its suffix-comparison state at input position $|p|$ with counter $r$, reaches a halted configuration within at most $|s|+1$ steps, with output the single Boolean indicating whether $|s|\le r$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $x$
$r$ is at most the length of $c$'s output
The running time is bounded by $|s|+1$
replaced:
For a split $x = p s$ of the input and a counter $r$ at most the captured
word's length, from the checker's comparison state at position $\abs{p}$
there is a time $t \le \abs{s} + 1$ such that after $t$ steps the checker has
halted with output the single bit recording whether $\abs{s} \le r$; the
empty suffix succeeds even with counter $0$.
